reasons.F: The barrow glade: the only signature effect that clearly reads from the game camera (a teal coil of streaming light over the barrows), with a standing-stone ring, crypts and headstones that give the area an identity of its own.
reasons.C: The fading well: the cleanest sacred ring of eleven standing stones plus lone stones and arches, the clearest landmark prop of the six; its breath of motes is faint from the camera.
reasons.D: The watch of towers: slender ruined towers and leaning ancients give the rims a silhouette none of the others has, and its well-glow coils and crackles; the palette is the same cold green-grey as the rest.

fixes.F: The ring is scattered as a prop set like any other; give it one fixed place at the pool so the landmark sits where the brief wants it (a layout or landmark change, not data).
fixes.C: Raise the motes' size and rate, or add a light layer, so the effect reads from the game camera.
fixes.D: Push the accent: from above it is indistinguishable from the other five.

notes: All six landed on nearly the same cold green-grey palette, so the whole-map view barely separates them; the directions varied the props and effects but not the colour. The landmark brief can't be met with data alone: a tileset scatters prop sets, so a ring 'round the well' needs a landmark placement in code. Two rules were too strict and were loosened after the run (catalog comment lines; a 300-line cap on the tileset), after which all six passed.
